build.reason: Both arms stopped for required design approval on build-feature and both passed build-bugfix. GPT-6 Sol was more efficient on the completed workload, but neither model satisfied both frozen workloads.

explore.reason: Both direct-model recovery arms returned the exact dependency chain. GPT-5.6 Luna was faster while GPT-6 Luna was cheaper in the observed cache state; one fixture provides no replacement signal.

general.reason: Both direct-model recovery arms stopped for required design approval on build-feature and both passed build-bugfix. GPT-6 Luna was slightly faster and much cheaper on the completed workload, but neither model satisfied both frozen workloads.

invalidated_calls.reason: OpenCode rejected direct execution of explore/general subagents and fell back to the default Build agent. These calls support no model comparison.

limitations: One attempt per model per workload does not establish reliability.
The feature fixture measures the unattended Superpowers approval contract as well as coding ability.
General uses direct model dispatch because OpenCode 1.18.31 cannot directly run the general subagent and that agent has no role-specific prompt.
The fixture checks are silent. Original Build verdicts rely on attempt-recorded exit statuses after sandbox deletion; recovery General verdicts retain both explicit exit records and final sandboxes.
Every dispatch carries a stale historical routing_profile_id from a pre-existing runner constant; direct model and variant targets establish valid-call identity.
Observed harness credits vary materially with cache state and are not reconciled against the GitHub billing interface.
